The representative is elected [[at-large]], because the state has only one congressional district, encompassing its entire territory. By area, Alaska's congressional district is the [[List of United States congressional districts by area|largest congressional district]] in the United States and the third-largest [[electoral district]] represented by a single member in the world, exceeded only by the [[Yakutsk constituency|Yakutsk]] district in Russia and [[Nunavut (electoral district)|Nunavut]] in Canada. On August 31, 2022, [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Mary Peltola]] defeated Republican former governor [[Sarah Palin]] in the [[2022 Alaska's at-large congressional district special election|special election]] to replace [[Don Young]], who died on March 18 of the same year, and was the longest serving Republican in the history of the House. Peltola became the first Democrat elected to the House of Representatives from Alaska since [[1972 United States House of Representatives election in Alaska|1972]], and the first [[Alaska Natives|Alaska Native]] in history to be elected to the [[United States House of Representatives]]. Peltola was defeated by [[Nick Begich III]] in 2024. It has a [[Cook Partisan Voting Index|partisan lean]] of R+6. ==History== The district was created when Alaska achieved statehood on January 3, 1959, and having existed uninterrupted ever since. Given the growth of population across the nation, Alaska is still entitled to only one seat in the House of Representatives. ===Voter registration=== {| class=wikitable ! colspan = 6 | Voter registration as of January 3, 2021{{Cite web|url=https://www.elections.alaska.gov/statistics/2021/JAN/VOTERS%20BY%20PARTY%20AND%20PRECINCT.htm|title=Alaska Voter Registration by Party/Precinct|access-date=May 18, 2023}} |- ! colspan = 2 | Party !
